items.note: Larrow Valley Cooperative Creamery Association, organized 1889 at Larrow Green; Gideon Vose first president to 1911; creamery built 1891.
Article VII quoted verbatim: paid by pounds of butterfat ascertained by test, not by weight of milk; test of the station where he delivers governs.
Quotes Falke: under payment by weight nothing that follows would have cost any man a dollar; calls Article VII the hinge.
Effie Loomis secretary, Hobart Sill buttermaker, Teague's ledger line ruled from 1905 (bookkeeper role conveyed). Dates for Loomis not given but are context.
Selby Vose appears nowhere in the batch's Section A - no mention of Gideon's son or the 1913 managership. Fully stated at B3, but credit never travels from B-G into Section A.
Station-gain line given from the 1898 account: 57,760 credited, 60,800 received, gain 3,040 lb, five and a quarter per cent, 'as usual' - existence, shape and 1898 origin all present.
Ostrey Hollow skimming station, seven miles up, built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed of Larrow Green (with the 'Ashlin creamery' slip correctly rejected).

Section A gives only 'weighed, sampled, tested thirty-one times a week and separated; cream down, skim back'. No composite sample, and nowhere in Section A is the reading mechanism stated - a fixed pipette charge read as a percent on the graduated neck. That mechanism appears only at C1(a), which cannot travel into Section A.
Ammon & Sons, Dairy Supply, Tarnet; invoice 14 April 1897; in use 1 May 1897, with the 1898 and 1899 rivals named and rejected on Orra's same-day entry.
Full invoice reproduced line by line, 6 doz. pipettes marked 17.6 c.c., total $77.93; $77.39 and five dozen both named as errors.

0.19 short of the truth, 'the same in February as in July'; and five hundredths in winter cannot carry nineteen hundredths in July. Keeps the 0.17 Hollow-vs-Green gap distinct from the 0.19 shortfall.

Quotes Vaught: the pipette is 'the one instrument the plant cannot check against anything else', and 'from inside nobody could see it'. The burette is not named as the required check inside Section A (only 'Ivy's burette sheet' in the document list), but the proposition is stated.

Gives Keddie born 1861 and tester from 4 May 1896, but Section A never states the twenty-nine seasons / 1896-1924 span, the 30 April 1925 dismissal, or the 1934 death. 'Kept on fourteen years' from 1911 is the nearest, and does not carry the end of his service.

The test book is identified and quoted throughout as Keddie's own bench record (first leaf, 1911 entries, summary leaf, 'A.K.' initials). The column list, the one hand and the crossed-and-initialed corrections are unbolded context and do not gate.
Both figures: 1896 average 3.80 on Sill's borrowed glass; 3.61 from 1898 'or within three hundredths of it every year' on the summary leaf, with the step placed at the change of glassware.
Pipette broke 8 May 1911, borrowed measure nine weeks to 10 July, tests at 3.80, return to 3.61 the day the station's own measure came back, and the '? - A.K.' quoted.
Married Orra Brant, Emmet Brant's sister - 'the tie that later put the tester at the biggest patron's table'.

The 1919 water circular is absent from Section A (only Grigg's 1919 reprint letter appears), and Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement is absent entirely. The circular is mentioned at B3, which cannot travel into Section A.
No death in 1934, no impoundment of the test book, no county historical rooms. The batch's narratives stop at 1911.
Granddaughter, stated flatly and correctly.

Derivation via Duncan (Ansel's son, b. 1894) to Ivy (b. 1931), cross-checked on the Chronicle's 'twenty-seven in October 1958'. Great-niece named as the two second-hand printings and rejected, including Falke's own retraction - hedged, so no deduction.
Second cousins with the full derivation: Emmet and Orra siblings, Roy and Duncan first cousins, Hazel and Ivy their children. 'First cousin once removed' named and defeated.

Abstention A08 taken correctly: full vs half siblings filed under 'what the sources leave open', with Roy and Hazel's opposed claims and the note that the twelve-year gap fits either. The degree is left unchanged (at worst 'half second cousins'), so the answer does not turn on it. No verdict sentence either way; no gullibility deduction.
Gideon Vose, his father - on Selby's own words plus Effie's 'son of the late president' and Kyle; the nephew claim named as Vira's and Rundle's and rejected.

Significance stated exactly as the key expects: Gideon wrote Article VII making the station's test decide every patron's pay, and his son ran the office that enforced it and accused the patrons. Also gives the Vose Jerseys at 4.56.

Abstention A01: 'No relationship ... is established', 'not proven', and explicitly 'nothing could settle it' since the diary pages before 1889 were not preserved. Leans to no-kinship but every verdict sentence carries a declining qualifier, so it is a correct abstention under the operational test; no -2.

States what is established: Vira and Cleve carry a cousinship from talk and cannot trace a line and may descend from one rumour; Duncan denies it flatly; no marriage, document or birth record connects the families; Orra's diary never names a Vose.
16.72 / 17.6 = 0.95; tests read 95 per cent of true, short one part in twenty. 16.27 named as the rival, rejected on five independent grounds - hedged, no deduction.
3.61 / 0.95 = 3.80, short 0.19. 3.16 and 0.21 both named and rejected.

40,000,000 lb over the 25 full years 1898-1922; 1,444,000 credited against 1,520,000 true; 76,000 lb not credited, cross-checked against 3,040 x 25. 44,000,000, 67,000 and 118,000 all named as errors.
76,000 x $0.25 = $19,000; award $3,800; ratio 0.20, one fifth. Both the money and the fraction given. $19,600, $3,500 and 27 cents named and rejected.
True test 3.60, true fat 7,200 lb, owed 360 lb, with two independent checks.
360 x $0.24 = $86.40, with the 1910 price sourced to Roy and the $90.00 alternative explicitly set aside.
